title: legal-redlines-scratchpad-avery-collins
content:
Purpose: quick personal scratchpad for common redlines + suggested negotiation talking points for inference service agreements (hosted/dedicated/private). Mostly shorthand - keep for reviews and handoffs.

High-level risks to flag (quick):
- Data use / model training: client must NOT be required to allow training on customer inputs. If provider wants to use data to improve models, require explicit opt-in or strong anonymization + notice + ability to opt-out.
- IP / outputs: clarify ownership of customer-generated outputs. Default ask: customer owns Outputs; provider gets a limited license to operate service.
- Model weights / models: vendor should NOT claim ownership of customer prompts or outputs. Also check language about ownership of derived models or fine-tuned variants.
- Confidentiality scope: ensure logs, telemetry, embeddings, prompts are Confidential Information. Define retention limits for logs.
- Security/compliance: require SOC2 Type II report annually; for regulated customers require BAA (HIPAA) or PCI scoping if relevant.
- Liability cap: generally capped to fees paid in previous 12 months - push to 12 months (not 6) and carve out gross negligence / willful misconduct and IP indemnity.
- Indemnity: reciprocal indemnities where possible; vendor indemnity for IP claims should be limited to claims resulting from vendor-supplied models or services (not customer data/instructions).
- SLA / remedies: spell out SLOs by deployment type (hosted vs dedicated vs private). For dedicated: 99.9% uptime SLO; define p95/p99 latency targets; service credits as sole remedy.
- Termination & transition: require 60-90 days transition assistance and export of customer data in standard formats. Define timeline for data retrieval after termination (30 days + secure delete).
- Subprocessors: vendor must provide subprocessors list + 30 days notice for new ones + ability to object for high-risk subprocessors.
- Encryption & keys: KMS support + customer-managed keys for private deployment or enterprise; ensure key control options; at minimum encryption at rest/in transit.
- Audit rights: limit to reasonable frequency and require NDA; for customers with compliance needs allow for third-party attestations or onsite audits subject to notice.
- Export controls & sanctions: ensure vendor represents compliance and right to suspend service if sanctions apply - but require notice where possible.

Clause-by-clause notes / suggested redlines (short):
1) Data usage / training clause:
   - Vendor proposes: "We may use Customer Data to improve models."
   - Redline: "Vendor may only use Customer Data to provide the Services and to improve the Services if Customer gives prior written consent, and any such use will be in aggregated/anonymized form and cannot be used to train models that will be sold to direct competitors."
   - Talking point: customers care about IP leakage and competitor exposure; offer analytics/ops-only use, not training.

2) Ownership of Outputs:
   - Vendor often tries to claim limited license back.
   - Redline: "Customer retains all right, title, and interest in and to Outputs. Vendor may store and use Outputs only to provide the Service and as allowed above re: anonymized analytics."

3) Liability / Cap:
   - Vendor default: cap = fees paid in prior 6 months; disclaimers for consequential damages.
   - Negotiation: ask for cap = prior 12 months fees for SaaS/hosted; for Dedicated consider a higher cap or carveouts for IP/personal data breaches. Carve out for bodily injury, death, and gross negligence.

4) SLA specifics:
   - Want separate metrics: availability (percent), p95/p99 token latency, error rate, and queue/backlog thresholds.
   - Remedies: service credits (define calculation) and requirement for root cause & mitigation plan for recurring breaches.

5) Data deletion & portability:
   - Require export within 30 days in structured format (JSON/CSV) plus certification of deletion within 60 days.

6) Security incident / breach notification:
   - Require notification within 72 hours for confirmed personal data breaches; weekly updates until resolved.

7) Audit/attestations:
   - Ask for annual SOC2 + pen test report; for very sensitive customers require BAA and right to request SOC2 + bridge letter.

8) Subprocessors & third parties:
   - Require list + right to object for subprocessors handling Personal Data or GPU infra in specific regions.

9) Exportability of model artifacts (Private deployments):
   - If vendor supplies model artifacts (weights), confirm license/usage rights, and ensure customer can continue to run locally after termination per agreed license.

10) Escrow / continuity:
   - For enterprise/dedicated: consider code/model escrow for change-of-control or insolvency. Also require runbook & minimum transfer support if vendor stops supporting a model.

Negotiation playbook (short bullets):
- Start by removing any broad "we can use your data to improve our models" language; propose opt-in training + anonymization + no-sale-to-competitors clause.
- Push for reciprocal mutual indemnities limited to negligence and IP breaches; vendor retains responsibility for vendor-controlled code/models.
- For high-risk customers, require BAA + customer-managed keys + on-prem/private deployment option.
- SLA: accept service credits as sole financial remedy for availability issues, but push for transparent measurement and monthly reporting + root cause commitments.
- Liability cap: try for 12 months fees; if vendor resists, get better carveouts and insurance commitments (cyber liability).

Unresolved questions / follow-ups:
- Confirm standard vendor data retention periods for logs/requests (default) - ask for 30-90 day log retention or per-customer settings.
- Is there a standard private deployment KMS integration guide? link to infra PR needed (JIRA-ENG-2045).
- Check if SOC2/pen test artifacts are shareable under NDA; add requested list to vendor security questionnaire.

Useful quick snippets to drop into redlines:
- "Vendor shall not use Customer Data to retrain or improve any models without Customer's prior written consent, which may be withheld in Customer's sole discretion."
- "Customer retains ownership of all Outputs; Vendor is granted a limited, non-exclusive license to use Outputs solely to provide the Services and for internal metrics/analytics in anonymized form."
- "For indemnity claims, the Cap shall not apply to claims arising from willful misconduct or gross negligence."

References / where to copy from internally:
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-REDLINE-34 (enterprise inference template)
- Jira: JIRA-ENG-2045 (private KMS integration work)
- GH PR: GITHUB-PR-5123 (SLA metric dashboard schema)
- Slack thread: #legal-contracts / thread id SLACK-C-0abcd (recent negotiation with Acme Corp)

Notes to self: keep these punchy and copy into first-pass SOW template. flag to SEs: ask customers early about training opt-in and KMS needs.

-- a.c.
